memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "Moses said to Aaron, 'Come to the altar and sacrifice your sin offering and your burnt offering and make atonement for yourself and the people; sacrifice the offering that is for the people and make atonement for them, as the LORD has commanded.'" - Lev 9:7 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Come to the altar. Two words that summarise Aaron's entire calling — and, in a sense, ours.

Notice the order carefully. Make atonement for yourself and the people. Himself first. Aaron could not carry others to God while neglecting his own standing before Him.

This is one of the most practical principles in Scripture for anyone who serves. You cannot sustainably give what you do not have. The parent teaching children to pray, the friend counselling someone in crisis, the leader carrying a congregation — all of them run dry if their own altar is neglected.

Paul told Timothy, Watch your life and doctrine closely. Persevere in them, because if you do, you will save both yourself and your hearers (1 Tim 4:16). Yourself first, then your hearers.

This is not selfishness. It is the reason flight attendants tell you to fit your own oxygen mask before helping others.

But notice too that Aaron did not stop with himself. Having dealt with his own need, he turned immediately to the people.

Attend to your own soul. Then give yourself away.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Am I trying to help others spiritually while neglecting my own walk with God?
2. Or have I turned inward, tending my own soul while ignoring people around me?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, keep my own altar burning, and then use me for others. Let me neither neglect myself nor serve only myself. Amen.
